items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: Well he did the Moody arrangements for the Monterey Jazz Festival... he did the Moody one. And those were his arrangements.

ctx.x: very proud of the one article that talked about him, Leonard Feather wrote the article in fact, about Gil Fuller. And he was very proud of that article, that at least somebody recognized his talents. And he was telling me all the things he did that he didn’t get credit for, and of course I found out later that he also was a fantastic liar in a lot of ways, and exaggerator, and he exaggerated a lot of his accomplishments. And I won’t say – I mean I don’t know to what degree he did, but I have since found out that…
I have a picture of an LP I had, “Last Train from Overbrook.” I think it was James Moody.

Yeah. Well he did the Moody arrangements for the Monterey Jazz Festival. Remember that? There were two albums that came out, because he was in charge of the Monterey Jazz Festival Orchestra for a while, and he did the Gillespie one, and then he did the Moody one. And those were his arrangements. I’ve yet to hear anybody dispute that, so I don’t know. Maybe somebody will at some point. But he said he did those. And they’re wonderful albums, both of them.
